active_question.title: Validate a fixed Agent-local executor identity with keep-id
active_question.summary: The fixed Agent-local execution identity paired with keep-id made both protected registered mounts writable while preserving rootless, non-root, no-network isolation.

current_hypothesis.statement: A fixed Agent-local execution identity paired with keep-id will make both registered worktree and protected output mounts writable while preserving non-root rootless isolation.
success_criteria: The generated Podman argv contains only the derived Agent UID:GID when the registered profile selects the sole approved identity mode.
The isolated acceptance retains all four expected artifacts, reports a non-root container identity, and leaves no source/worktree/container residue.
failure_criteria: Either registered bind mount remains unwritable under the derived Agent identity.
Validation requires privileged containers, rootful Podman, provider access, or unbounded Podman options.
primary_metrics: container-visible mount ownership and write outcomes
baseline_refs: real-host executor failure: disposable worktree permission denied

active_experiment.purpose: Validate the fixed Agent-local identity policy in the existing isolated rootless executor acceptance fixture.
active_experiment.design: Add one literal Agent-local identity mode accepted only with keep-id, prove fixed argv derivation locally, then repeat the one registered no-network patch-and-test acceptance with a fresh idempotency key.
active_experiment.backend: existing RelayMe test host rootless Podman

findings.summary: With keep-id, Agent-owned mounts are visible as the Agent numeric identity while the image process remains a different primary identity. Protected output writes fail; the current group-writable disposable worktree and existing test file remain writable through a supplementary Agent group.
evidence: Both namespace-map forms were captured from inside the container and from a live keep-id container.
Fresh ordinary and disposable-worktree probes used network none, a read-only root filesystem, no provider material, and confirmed the existing fixed test file behavior.
All temporary containers, worktrees, and outputs were removed.

findings.summary: The fixed Agent-local identity mode paired with keep-id produced the Agent identity inside the rootless container and made both protected mounts writable without adding privilege, network, or client authority.
evidence: Local regression rejects unsupported, unpaired, client-supplied, and brief-supplied identity controls.
The isolated real-host fixed task retained all bounded review artifacts, preserved the source repository, cleaned its worktree/container, and replayed the retained result.
No provider credential, provider egress, or production resource was used.

candidate_next_experiments.summary: The isolated non-provider executor acceptance passed with the fixed Agent-local identity. Provider-enabled testing remains a separate, not-yet-authorized step.
